audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer calls the cage Yorick's E in eight places — "his E mist-cage is fully ranged", "walk out of the E wall", "his E cage plus Maiden's zone damage", "never let his E wall pin you against terrain", "Yorick's E mist-cage limits your movement", "his E mist-cage has no wall", "Trap Tahm Kench ... with E mist-cage". The full layer for the same matchup correctly calls it Dark Procession.
audit.why: Dark Procession is Yorick's W: a destructible wall, 20/18/16/14/12s, 600 range. His E is Mourning Mist, a different ability entirely. The two layers of the same matchup contradict each other, and the content layer also omits the single most important property of the wall — it is DESTRUCTIBLE. A Tahm Kench told only to "walk out of the E wall" never learns he can simply attack it down, which is the actual escape when he is caged against his own tower.
audit.corrected: Dark Procession (W): destructible wall, 20/18/16/14/12s. Break it rather than walking around it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mourning Mist is never mentioned anywhere in either layer of this matchup.
audit.why: It is the ability that starts every Yorick trade and the matchup does not know it exists. Mourning Mist is a 700-range globule on 12/11/10/9/8s that reduces armour, damages, SLOWS and MARKS the target — and Riot's text is explicit that summoned units gain move speed moving toward marked targets. So the mist is what turns a loose ghoul pack into a committed all-in, and dodging it is what prevents the trade from happening at all. Against a champion whose whole plan is to walk in and stack, that is the single most useful thing to know.
audit.corrected: Mourning Mist (E), 700 range, 12s at rank 1: armour shred, slow, and a mark that makes every ghoul sprint at you. Dodge it and the all-in does not start.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: 45.77% over 804 games is the LOWEST win rate of all 71 Tahm Kench top matchups, yet diff is "EVEN", diffRating is 6/10, and the level chart hands Tahm Kench 4 of 7 stages against Yorick's 1. phases[6].why even says "your side-lane pattern is at full power" at two items.
audit.why: The chart and the rating both contradict the data and the matchup's own prose. content.late already states plainly that at two items "you cannot 1v1 him on a pushed side wave", so phases[6].why claiming full power in the side lane is a direct internal contradiction at exactly the stage the win rate says is worst. For scale: Gwen at 48.97% is rated HARD 8.5/10 in this same file, so Yorick at 45.77% sitting at EVEN 6/10 is out of line with the dataset's own convention.
audit.corrected: diff HARD (tone to match). Chart should read Tahm Kench, Tahm Kench, Tahm Kench, Skill, Skill, Yorick, Yorick — he takes over at Maiden and never gives it back.
sources: champ-data/tahmkench.full.js — comparison against gwen, wukong, riven ratings

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid says "Abyssal Voyage means he cannot freely int-push and recall without you responding globally, and you can use the pool to bail if Maiden shows up". spikes[2].text and wants.you[2] repeat the global claim.
audit.why: Two separate fabrications in one sentence. Abyssal Voyage is Tahm Kench's removed pre-2020 W — the live W is Abyssal Dive, a short-range knockup on 21/20/19/18/17s with no global component. And "the pool" is not a Tahm Kench ability at all; it appears to be Vladimir's Sanguine Pool. The level-6 macro plan here is built on two abilities the champion does not have.
audit.corrected: Tahm Kench answers a split with Teleport and jungle pressure, not with a global. Level 6 is Devour.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early, whys[2], spikes[1].text and wants.you[0] all run "a stun into Devour" / "the Q stun into Devour" off one set of three stacks.
audit.why: Riot's Tongue Lash text says that at 3 stacks the target is stunned AND the stacks are consumed; the passive says three stacks are the requirement to Devour. One charge, two spenders. Against Yorick the correct spender is unambiguous — Devour removes him from his ghouls for the full duration, which a short stun does not.
audit.corrected: Spend the three stacks on Devour. The Q stun is the worse option in this matchup.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — P and Q descriptions

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Dark Procession as matchup-defining but gives no number, and nothing anywhere states Last Rites' cooldown.
audit.why: Dark Procession is 20/18/16/14/12s — the longest cooldown in his laning kit and the only real commitment window. Mourning Mist is 12/11/10/9/8s and Last Rites is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s with an auto-reset and a heal attached. Those three numbers are what let a player time a walk-up instead of guessing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing flags Last Rites as an anti-heal target.
audit.why: Last Rites heals Yorick on every empowered attack on a 6s cooldown at rank 1 and is also an auto-attack reset, so it is both his sustain and his burst tell. The missing-interactions file flags this matchup for both needs-antiheal and autoreset-burst-tell, and neither appears in the text.
audit.corrected: Last Rites heals and resets his auto every 6s — Grievous Wounds matters, and the wind-up is the tell.
sources: champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json — needs-antiheal and autoreset-burst-tell, tahmkench vs yorick

edits.before: Level 1 is yours — Tongue Lash outranges every tool Yorick has pre-ghoul, so slow him on his walk-up to Last Rites and deny the CS he needs to fuel his ghoul stacks. The moment you hit 3 An Acquired Taste stacks, that Q stun is a free punish: he has no dash and no disengage, so a stun into Devour eats his health bar while his ghouls swing helplessly outside. Do not let him stack three ghouls before you trade — the ghoul damage in a long fight is meaningful — so keep exchanges short, stun-Devour and back out while your Thick Skin converts the ghoul hits into grey health you heal between trades.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours — Tongue Lash outranges every tool Yorick has pre-ghoul, so slow him on his walk-up to Last Rites and deny the CS he needs to fuel his ghoul stacks. His real opener is Mourning Mist, the E: a 700-range globule that shreds armour, slows, and marks you so every ghoul sprints in. Dodge it and the trade never starts. Do not let him stack three ghouls before you trade, keep exchanges short, and spend three stacks on Devour rather than the stun while Thick Skin banks the ghoul hits as grey health you heal back between trades.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are the flat zone where Yorick starts threatening: his E mist-cage is fully ranged and zones you off a big section of the lane, and his ghoul count during a fight starts to add up. Do not let him cage you against your own tower — hug the lane's center so you have room to walk out of the E wall, and save your Q slow to interrupt his Last Rites cast when he goes for stacks. Level 6 is your reprieve: Abyssal Voyage means he cannot freely int-push and recall without you responding globally, and you can use the pool to bail if Maiden shows up before your jungler does. Keep stacking An Acquired Taste in short poke trades; you do not need a clean kill here, just deny him a free shove.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are the flat zone where Yorick starts threatening: Dark Procession is his W, not his E — a wall on a 20s cooldown at rank 1 that zones you off a big section of the lane — and his ghoul count during a fight starts to add up. Do not let him cage you against your own tower; hug the lane's centre so you have room, and remember the wall is destructible, so hit it rather than walking the long way. Mourning Mist is the E, 12s at rank 1, and that is what actually opens his trades. Keep stacking An Acquired Taste in short poke trades; you do not need a clean kill here, just deny him a free shove. Last Rites is a 6s auto-reset that heals him, so bring Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: Once Yorick has two items and Maiden is permanently on the map, the honest truth is you cannot 1v1 him on a pushed side wave — his E cage plus Maiden's zone damage plus ghoul swarm outputs more sustained damage than your Thick Skin grey-health cycle can handle. Your job shifts to locking him down in skirmishes before Maiden arrives: the Devour still removes him from a teamfight entirely and your Abyssal Voyage lets you collapse on objectives. Never chase him into a split-push corridor and never let his E wall pin you against terrain — fight him only when your team is present and can kill the ghouls, or intercept the Maiden while he is busy dying to the stun-Devour in a fight.
edits.after: Once Yorick has two items and Maiden is permanently on the map, the honest truth is you cannot 1v1 him on a pushed side wave — his W cage plus Maiden's zone damage plus ghoul swarm outputs more sustained damage than your Thick Skin grey-health cycle can handle. Your job shifts to locking him down in skirmishes before Maiden arrives: Devour still removes him from a teamfight entirely, and Teleport rather than any global of your own is how you collapse on objectives. Never chase him into a split-push corridor and never let Dark Procession pin you against terrain — it is destructible, so break it — and fight him only with your team present to clear the ghouls.

notes: LEVEL CHART — I could not fully fix this and the user must apply it by hand. The packet defect is real: 45.77% is the lowest win rate of all 71 Tahm Kench top matchups, but the chart gives Tahm Kench 4 of 7 stages. The correct chart is Tahm Kench / Tahm Kench / Tahm Kench / Skill / Skill / Yorick / Yorick — he takes over when Maiden lands and never gives it back. I did not propose those side edits because "Tahm Kench" -> "Yorick" is a 10-to-6 character change and the applier's +/-10% length band would reject it; the same blocks diffRating 6/10 -> 8.5/10. I did change diff EVEN -> HARD and the matching tone, both exactly length-neutral, and rewrote phases[6].why, breakdown.difficulty and breakdown.late so the prose no longer claims Tahm Kench is at "full power" in the side lane at two items while content.late says the opposite three lines away. SUGGESTION FOR THE APPLIER: exempt short enum-like fields (win[], phases[].side, diff, diffRating, carryRating, spikes[].when) from the length band — they are labels, not prose, and right now they cannot be corrected at all.
